newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom up on renewed sale talk.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom up on renewed sale talk.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd shares rallied on Wednesday on rumours a Hong Kong blue chip or China's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (MPT) may take a stake in the utility.
Hongkong Telecom shares were up HK$0.25 at HK$14.35 just before the midday break after rising more than six percent on Tuesday.
Both Hutchison Whampoa Ltd and MPT have been tipped to buy into Hongkong Telecom, Mansion House Research said in a report on Wednesday.
"Basically it's the same rumour mill that's been going on for the past few months," said an analyst with a European firm.
"If it's market rumour, then we won't comment," a Hongkong Telecom spokeswoman told Reuters.
The company is due report its results for the year to March 31 on Thursday.
The analyst saw potential benefits for Hutchison from an investment in Hongkong Telecom, but Morgan Stanley's Jeff Camp disagreed.
"Hutchison actually has quite a decent telecom business of its own," Camp said.
Setting up its own local network would be far cheaper than buying into Hongkong Telecom's network, he said.
DBS Securities analyst Philip Tulk said it was hard to assess the benefits to Hutchison of buying into Hongkong Telecom. "It's not a simple evaluation," Tulk said.
Hutchison shares were off HK$0.50 at HK$60.75 on Wednesday.
